subtasks.title: Precheck skip-set + scoped/fast check preference
subtasks.prompt: Implement PLAN.md sections 1 and 2 (Findings 1 and 2). In src/bun/repo-profile.ts: add `export type CheckName = "typecheck" | "lint" | "test" | "build"`; add an optional `skipChecks?: ReadonlySet<CheckName>` opt to `renderProjectCommands` that drops a check's line entirely when present (keep the existing 'no known commands' early return keyed on the UNFILTERED command set, per §1a); add four new nullable RepoProfile fields (`typecheckScoped`, `lintScoped`, `testScoped`, `buildScoped`) populated only when the corresponding `<check>:changed` script exists AND the full check script also exists (canonical label, not the alias that satisfied the full command — see §2b); update EMPTY_PROFILE; make renderProjectCommands prefer the scoped command over the full one per line (§2c). In src/bun/pipeline-precheck.ts: add `precheckPassedChecks(summary): Set<CheckName>` per §1b (import CheckName as a type from repo-profile.ts). In src/bun/orchestrator.ts: reorder `pipelinePromptExtras` so the O-5 precheck read happens before the project-commands block and feed `precheckPassedChecks(precheckSummary)` into `renderProjectCommands` as `skipChecks` (§1c) — precheckSummary stays null for non-testing stages and unset precheck, so skipChecks stays undefined there. Add `"test:changed": "bun scripts/test-changed.ts"` to package.json scripts, and create scripts/test-changed.ts per §2d (base ref resolution, changed-file detection via TEST_PATH_PATTERNS convention + sibling *.test.ts lookup, dedupe, run `bun test <files>` via Bun.spawn, exit 0 with a note when nothing affected). Do NOT add a typecheck:changed script for this repo (§2e — document the rationale only in the docs subtask, not here). Update/add tests in src/bun/repo-profile.test.ts, src/bun/pipeline-precheck.test.ts, and src/bun/orchestrator-pipeline-token.test.ts exactly as described in PLAN.md §5 (first three bullet groups only — skip the pipeline-prompts.test.ts bullet, that's a different subtask). Everything must be fail-open: any error deriving skipChecks, or a profile with no :changed scripts, renders byte-identical output to before this change. Do not touch precheckPasses, testerSkipEnabled, or precheckEnabled.

subtasks.title: Build-child debugging consolidation guidance
subtasks.prompt: Implement PLAN.md section 3 (Finding 3) in src/bun/pipeline-prompts.ts only. Add a `CHILD_DEBUG_CONSOLIDATE_TOOL_CALLS = 40` constant near the other sizing knobs (e.g. DECOMPOSE_SINGLE_SUBTASK_MAX_FILES), documented as a rough prose-only guideline (no enforcement — matches the SPEC non-goal against sandboxing/technical enforcement). In `childBuildPrompt` only (not `buildingPrompt`, which is out of scope), splice a new paragraph between `${subtask.prompt}` and the existing 'When you're done, commit…' paragraph: it must (a) direct the build step to verify using this repo's own existing typecheck/lint/test commands and relevant e2e specs instead of starting a second long-running process of its own (e.g. a duplicate dev server), (b) state that if it genuinely cannot verify without a running app instance, it should report that as a limitation in its final message rather than improvise one, and (c) tell it that once it's well past what a change this size should normally take (rough guide: more than ~40 tool calls, or repeated failed attempts at the same fix), it should stop, commit what's working, and clearly state what remains unresolved rather than iterating indefinitely — worded so it doesn't create false urgency for a normally-proceeding small task. Keep the added text tight: the existing 'fixed overhead stays well inside the claude argv budget' test asserts total prompt overhead stays under 2048 bytes — do not raise that ceiling, size the wording to fit. Update src/bun/pipeline-prompts.test.ts per PLAN.md §5's last bullet group: assert the new guidance appears via stable fixed-string substring checks (e.g. wording equivalent to 'say so as a limitation', 'stop: commit what's working'), and only touch the existing byte-budget test if the math requires it.
